subject: Citywide Residential Zoning Reform
overview: City Council President Zac Bears discussed the ongoing citywide rezoning effort and the decision to extend the timeline for the residential district proposal. The interview addressed housing density, developer accountability, and potential impacts on the school system.

items.title: Introduction
items.summary: City Council President Zac Bears introduced himself and discussed his local restaurant preferences.

items.title: Rationale for Zoning Statement
items.summary: Bears explained his decision to extend the zoning review process by five to six months to refocus on the Council's original residential proposal following community concerns regarding Community Development Board recommendations.

items.title: Zoning Misinformation and Comprehensive Planning
items.summary: The discussion addressed misconceptions about the elimination of single-family housing and the role of the 2023 Comprehensive Plan in promoting smart growth.

items.title: Legislative Process and Neighborhood Specifics
items.summary: Bears detailed the legal authority of the City Council in zoning matters and explained how residential proposals are tailored to specific neighborhood characteristics and transit hubs.

items.title: Developer Accountability and Market Incentives
items.summary: The conversation focused on using zoning to incentivize modest multi-family units over large single-family homes while implementing new requirements for open space and developer linkage fees.

items.title: School Enrollment and Capacity Concerns
items.summary: Bears addressed concerns regarding school overcrowding, citing demographic trends and the historical impact of selling city-owned school properties.
